verdict.rationale: Kimi ships an official terminal CLI, Kimi Code CLI. Users start it with `kimi`, sign in with `/login`, and the agent can read code, edit files, run commands and search the web autonomously. The CLI also exposes ACP for editor integration, and a probe confirms the docs are live and that the CLI comes bundled with the Kimi membership. A community user notes that using OpenCode instead of the Kimi CLI hurt performance, which indirectly confirms the CLI exists and is used. missing for 10: direct independent hands-on evaluation of the CLI itself, detailed command/flag reference documentation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Chat with AI in the terminal, letting it read code, edit files, execute commands, search the web, and autonomously complete development tasks.
run `kimi` in the terminal to start; on first use, log in to the Kimi Code platform with the `/login` command to complete the connection
Other editors such as JetBrains and Zed can connect via CLI's ACP protocol.
